thread:
tina: I opened a docs PR for the migration guide + SDK usage snippet. CI is failing — linkcheck reports an internal anchor miss and mdspell + vale also flagged a couple items. can someone help triage quickly?

docs-ci-bot: Running checks for PR #3042: linkcheck, mdspell, vale, markdownlint, preview-build.

lee: I'll take the linkcheck. which anchor is 404?

tina: linkcheck says `#configure-private-network` in migration.md doesn't exist when preview builds the site. locally the header exists though.

marco: sometimes the static site generator normalizes anchors (spaces, punctuation). did you use an explicit header id or a duplicate header elsewhere?

tina: header is `## Configuring the private network (VPC)` — guess the generated anchor is `configuring-the-private-network-vpc`. I linked to `configure-private-network`. oops.

lee: easy fix, updating the cross-doc link to the generated anchor. pushing a one-line change.

marco: vale flagged `avoid using we` in the troubleshooting section: "We suggest checking KV cache settings." rule GOV-VOICE. should be active wording.

ryan: swap to imperative: `Check the KV cache settings.` keeps it concise and appeases vale.

tina: updated wording and pushed. also fixed a typo `enviroment` -> `environment` in sdk/snippets.md per mdspell.

docs-ci-bot: Re-running checks after new commits...

docs-ci-bot: linkcheck: one remaining internal anchor mismatch: `#onprem-install` referenced from getting-started.md.

lee: that anchor was renamed to `on-premises-installation` in migration.md recently. I'll add an alias anchor in the markdown (HTML comment with id) to preserve old links. pushing now.

marco: markdownlint warns about MD041 (first line in file should be a top-level header) in migration.md — we accidentally added a short note above the H1. move it below or convert to blockquote.

tina: moved the note to a blockquote under the H1 and pushed.

docs-ci-bot: mdspell: no issues. vale: still failing — GOV-VOICE at paragraph 4 (suggested stronger verb).

marco: paste the sentence?

tina: "We try to keep model parity across deployments."

ryan: change to active: `Keep model versions consistent across deployments.`

tina: done. pushed.

docs-ci-bot: All checks passed. Preview built at https://deploy-preview-3042.docs.redwood.ai/ — manual sanity check recommended.

lee: preview looks good. anchors and snippets render. small CSS nit for code block padding but not blocking.

marco: timing check — is this needed for the 1.6 release doc cut? release window closes at 15:30 UTC.

tina: yes, we'd like it merged before the cutoff. if CI stays green and one reviewer approves we can merge.

ryan: approving now. :+1:

lee: approving as well.

tina: thanks all. merging now. /merge

deploy-bot: Merge queued. Starting post-merge preview deploy.

deploy-bot: Preview successfully deployed at https://deploy-preview-3042.docs.redwood.ai/ — sanity-check anchors under "Configuring the private network (VPC)" and SDK snippet examples.

tina: verified anchor alias works, snippet examples render properly in both dark and light theme. all green.

marco: follow-up: can we add a lightweight CI check that validates internal anchor targets exist using the same anchor-generation rules as the site generator? I'd rather not rely on manual fixes.

lee: +1. I'll open an issue and suggest a small script run in linkcheck job to emulate hugo/markdown anchor normalization. tagging eng-infra/ci.

ryan: filed https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/issues/529 — short proposal and sample regex. thanks team for the quick turnaround :rocket:
